### Context

### Performance
- [x] No N+1 patterns
- [x] No unbounded operations
- [x] Pagination on list endpoints

### Verification
- [x] Tests pass
- [x] Build succeeds
- [x] Manual verification done (if applicable)

---

### Detailed Review Findings

#### 1. Correctness & Logic
- **Lexicographical Monotonic IDs (`revert.ts`)**: Reviewed the `parentID >= input.messageID` comparison logic in the revert handler. Since the `ascending` helper generates IDs with a fixed-length prefix (`msg_`), fixed-width (12-char) hex timestamps, and monotonic counters, string comparison guarantees correct chronological ordering. It is safe to compare these IDs lexicographically to check if assistant messages were started after the target message.
- **Accessor Access Corrected (`submit.ts` & `session.tsx`)**: Resolved the bugs where `sync` and `sdk` properties were accessed directly (`sync.data` and `sdk.client`). These are Solid signals/accessors and must be evaluated as functions (`sync()` and `sdk()`). They have been fixed and validated via typecheck.

#### 2. Readability & Coding Guidelines
- **Removed `any` Type Cast (`index.tsx`)**: Found and fixed a style violation in `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx` (line 1565), where `parts` array map parameters were cast to `any`. This was replaced with a proper TypeScript array shape cast (`Array<{ type: string; text?: string; synthetic?: boolean }>`) to respect the project's **"Avoid using the `any` type"** guideline.

#### 3. Performance & Resource Safety
- **Interrupt Polling (`processor.ts`)**: Looked at the mid-stream interrupt check loop utilizing `Effect.sleep("50 millis")`. While periodic polling is used, this loop is raced against the active LLM stream using `Effect.raceFirst`. When the stream completes or errors, `raceFirst` immediately cancels the polling fiber, preventing any background leakages or stray timers.

### Verdict
- [x] **Approve** — Ready to merge

Yes that's the new Queue mode. Queue on `dev` is currently more similar to Wait & Steer.

  • Halt/Steer & Wait/Steer: These bypass the idle check and push the prompt to the backend immediately to  request an interruption (either mid-stream or at the next tool boundary).

Offending tool: sanity_patch_documents — the schema uses internal $ref with relative paths (#/properties/...) instead of #/$defs/..., which Moonshot's validator rejects.

Hey @kitlangton — any update on this? It's been 16 days since filing and it's still blocking all browser-based clients from using the Zen/Go API entirely.

The fix is straightforward on paper — the gateway isn't responding to OPTIONS preflight requests, so they fall through to the frontend SPA router which returns a 404 HTML page instead of CORS headers. Same root cause as #10047 where basic auth was blocking OPTIONS — just at a different layer in the routing stack. The gateway needs to handle OPTIONS with proper CORS headers (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, GET, OPTIONS`, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type`) before requests hit the SPA router.

I've confirmed this is still reproducible:
```
OPTIONS /zen/go/v1/chat/completions → HTTP 404 (full SPA HTML page, zero CORS headers)
POST   /zen/go/v1/chat/completions → HTTP 401 ("Model test is not supported" — backend alive)
```

Happy to test if you push a branch. Until this is fixed, anyone trying to use OpenCode from browser-based clients (web UIs, custom frontends, AI chat platforms, etc.) is completely blocked.
